gap: No result ChatGPT got states a price for any plate, and none states that Prusa's Smooth PEI sheet, the one Prusa calls best for PLA, is also the cheapest of Prusa's three sheets today: $29.74, against $33.99 for Textured and $39.94 for Satin (prusa3d.com, 2026-11-17).
standout_why: I read four pages ChatGPT got: help.prusa3d.com PLA (cited), help.prusa3d.com flexible steel sheets guidepost (cited), nozzlenotes.com build plates (2026-10-14, updated 2026-11-11) and 3dadapt.com smooth vs textured vs satin (2026-10-09). None gives a price. The guidepost says outright that it lists no prices. nozzlenotes and 3dadapt rank the surfaces (textured as the all-round pick, smooth as a good PLA choice, satin for switching) but never say what each costs.
decides: For a Prusa owner who prints only PLA, the price backs up ChatGPT's 'If you print exclusively PLA, smooth PEI may actually be better.' Smooth is the surface Prusa says gives the best PLA adhesion, and it is also the cheapest sheet: $4.25 less than Textured and $10.20 less than Satin. Satin's extra cost only pays for easier PETG printing. ChatGPT's overall pick of textured PEI loses on PLA: Prusa's own Textured sheet page warns that PLA prints with a small contact area may need a brim and that large footprints may warp. For Bambu owners the BIQU CryoGrip Pro, which we list, is priced on BIQU's US store today, but I could not price Bambu's own plates. Bambu's store returned HTTP 402 to my fetches, so the Bambu price comparison is still open.

findings.note: Prusa says it offers 'an optimal level of adhesion, especially when printing PLA and PETG'. Do not clean it with acetone. Where it loses for PLA-only buyers: it costs $10.20 more than Smooth ($39.94 − $29.74), and Prusa's PLA article ranks satin and smooth together for adhesion.
